APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-014.statement: An `ANY_OF` group with at least one applicable member MUST evaluate as `APPROVED` when at least one applicable member is approved; it MUST evaluate as `REJECTED` only when every applicable member is rejected; otherwise it MUST evaluate as `PENDING`.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-014.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-014

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-015.statement: A `PENDING` member or voter MUST NOT be interpreted as an abstention, rejection, or approval.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-015.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-015

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-016.statement: An ordered Approval Stage list MUST evaluate stages in declared order and MUST NOT make a later stage actionable before every earlier stage is approved.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-016.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-016

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-017.statement: Groups declared within the same Approval Stage MUST be parallel for composition purposes. Their order MUST determine deterministic observation order only and MUST NOT establish prerequisite ordering.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-017.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-017

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-018.statement: A staged composition MUST evaluate as `APPROVED` only when every stage is approved, `REJECTED` when the first non-approved stage is rejected, and `PENDING` when the first non-approved stage is pending.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-018.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-018

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-019.statement: A pending staged composition MUST report all and only the pending, applicable Requirements reachable through exclusively pending groups in its first pending stage. It MUST visit that stage's root groups in declared order and recursively visit each pending group's members in declared order, reporting each Requirement identifier once at its first eligible occurrence. It MUST exclude later stages and approved, rejected, or entirely inapplicable group branches. An approved or rejected composition MUST report no actionable Requirements.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-019.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-019

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-020.statement: Composition state observations MUST NOT be treated as proof of which Approval Decision satisfied a Requirement or which subject facts were bound to that Decision.

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-021.statement: Composition evaluation MUST reuse Core 2.0 current-effectiveness semantics for withdrawn, expired, superseded, stale-fact, stale-revision, and ineligible Decisions.

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-022.statement: A structurally valid Approval Composition with no applicable Approval Requirements after explicit applicability evaluation MUST return `APPROVED`, meaning no approval is currently required. That outcome MUST NOT create or imply an approving Decision; it MUST remain distinguishable from evidence that a voter approved.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-022.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-022

APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-023.statement: An Approval Stage MUST omit entirely inapplicable groups from its outcome evaluation. With at least one applicable group, the stage MUST evaluate as `APPROVED` when every applicable group is approved, `REJECTED` when any applicable group is rejected, and `PENDING` otherwise. A structurally valid stage with no applicable groups MUST evaluate as `APPROVED`, meaning it imposes no current approval obligation and does not itself block progression to a later stage.
APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-023.title: APPROVAL-COMPOSITION-023

It MUST evaluate caller-declared relevant facts and any expiration under Approval Validity using explicit required context. Expired or fact-stale valid evidence MUST return `INEFFECTIVE`; otherwise it MUST return `EFFECTIVE`. Without supplied lifecycle history this observation MUST NOT claim lifecycle-aware effectiveness. A separately documented facts-only helper MAY remain available, but MUST NOT be used as the complete concrete evaluation.

APPROVAL-DECISION-012.statement: Before concrete Requirement evaluation returns an outcome, Actor eligibility MUST be validated for every structurally valid supplied Decision that identifies the evaluated Requirement, including a Decision excluded from current effectiveness by withdrawal, Decision supersession, Requirement supersession, expiration, stale facts or revision, or another decisive Decision. A valid eligibility declaration excluding the Actor MUST use `FINKORE_APPROVAL_INELIGIBLE_ACTOR`. A supplied Decision identifying another Requirement within the same history scope defined by **APPROVAL-DECISION-013** MUST still receive complete structural validation, but MUST NOT be tested against the evaluated Requirement's eligibility rule and MUST NOT affect its outcome. Evaluation MUST NOT invent an absent Requirement registry or eligibility rule for that unrelated Decision. A Decision from another context or subject is foreign-scope invalid evidence under **APPROVAL-DECISION-013**, not an unrelated Decision under this requirement.

APPROVAL-DECISION-013.statement: At the bounded detached-record boundary, every concrete Requirement MUST supply a nonempty opaque approval `contextId` together with its identity and exact subject reference, and every Decision MUST supply a `requirementRef` containing that `contextId`, the nonempty opaque Requirement identity, and the exact bounded subject reference. Every supplied Decision collection or history MUST be scoped to exactly one `contextId` and exact subject reference. Within that scope, a history MAY contain Decisions for more than one Requirement identity, and each Decision's `requirementRef.requirementId` MUST match its own retained Requirement identity. A candidate Decision at record or single-Decision evaluation MUST match the supplied Requirement's context, Requirement identity, and subject exactly. For Requirement evaluation over a collection, the history context and subject MUST match the evaluated Requirement, while only Decisions whose scoped Requirement identity also matches are selected for its eligibility, effectiveness, and outcome. Equal facts MUST NOT repair a context, Requirement, subject-type, or subject-identity mismatch. Missing or malformed scope, a Decision from a foreign context or subject, or another mismatched scoped association MUST use `FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_DECISION` and MUST preserve supplied Decision and lifecycle histories. Context identity is supplied and governed by the composing domain; FinKore requires no global registry.
APPROVAL-DECISION-013.title: APPROVAL-DECISION-013

APPROVAL-QUORUM-006.statement: An `N_OF_M` group with at least one explicitly applicable voting member whose threshold is not met MUST evaluate as `REJECTED` when the number of distinct effective approvals plus remaining pending applicable voting members is less than the declared `N`; otherwise it MUST evaluate as `PENDING`.

APPROVAL-QUORUM-007.statement: Each `N_OF_M` member MUST reference an Approval Requirement and MUST explicitly declare exactly one voter Actor identity; it MUST NOT reference a child Approval Group or leave voter identity to be inferred from subsequent Decisions, a role, or a group.

APPROVAL-QUORUM-009.statement: For an applicable quorum member, currently effective eligible Decisions by its declared voter for its referenced Requirement and current subject context MUST NOT include both satisfying and rejecting outcomes under that Requirement's outcome mapping. Evaluation MUST NOT resolve the conflict by Decision order, timestamp order, or an implicit preference for approval or rejection; only explicit lifecycle or current-effectiveness evidence may remove it. Repeated effective Decisions with the same mapped outcome MUST NOT by themselves constitute conflicting evidence.
APPROVAL-QUORUM-009.title: APPROVAL-QUORUM-009

APPROVAL-QUORUM-010.statement: Each applicable quorum member's state MUST be determined only from currently effective eligible Decisions matching its declared voter, referenced Requirement, and current subject context, using the Requirement's declared outcome mapping. After required validation, at least one satisfying Decision with no rejecting Decision MUST give that member `APPROVED`; at least one rejecting Decision with no satisfying Decision MUST give it `REJECTED`; no effective matching Decision MUST give it `PENDING`. Quorum capacity and actionable-member selection MUST use this member-specific state; another Actor's Decision or an aggregate Requirement observation MUST NOT replace it.

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-004.statement: A lifecycle event that withdraws a Decision MUST make only the identified Decision ineffective for current evaluation and MUST NOT remove or rewrite the withdrawn Decision.

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-005.statement: Withdrawal requests MUST identify exactly one committed Decision and MUST be rejected when the target is missing, ambiguous, already withdrawn, or already superseded.

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-006.statement: Withdrawal does not define authorization, delegation, or RBAC; when an implementation validates the withdrawal Actor against the affected Requirement, eligibility MUST be evaluated using the Requirement's declared eligibility boundary.

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-008.statement: Expiration instants and evaluation instants MUST identify unambiguous instants using the portable timestamp convention.

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-009.statement: A Decision is expired when the evaluation instant is equal to or later than the Decision's expiration instant. Equivalent offsets MUST compare by instant, not by lexical representation.

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-010.statement: A lifecycle event that supersedes a Decision MUST make the superseded Decision ineffective for current evaluation while preserving both historical Decisions and the supersession observation.

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-012.statement: Failed lifecycle operations and failed current-effectiveness evaluations MUST leave committed Decisions and lifecycle events unchanged.
APPROVAL-VALIDITY-012.title: APPROVAL-VALIDITY-012

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-013.statement: Before returning a concrete Requirement evaluation outcome, an implementation MUST validate required expiration context for every currently considered Decision, independently of Decision order or a decisive outcome. For this purpose, a currently considered Decision identifies the evaluated Requirement and is not excluded by committed withdrawal, Decision supersession, or Requirement supersession. Fact/revision staleness MUST NOT waive required expiration context for these Decisions. A structurally valid Decision for another Requirement in the same context and subject scope, or a lifecycle-excluded Decision, MUST NOT require an evaluation instant solely because it has an expiration. A foreign-context or foreign-subject Decision is invalid scoped evidence under **APPROVAL-DECISION-013**, not unrelated evidence that can be excluded. All supplied Decision and lifecycle structure MUST still be validated, including excluded evidence. Missing or malformed required context MUST use `FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_CONTEXT`. This rule does not define a total priority among unrelated concrete Approval failures.
APPROVAL-VALIDITY-013.title: APPROVAL-VALIDITY-013

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-014.statement: Before record, lifecycle mutation, or current-effectiveness evaluation reuses supplied committed lifecycle history, the implementation MUST validate supported discriminators, required field structure, the single context-and-subject scope defined by **APPROVAL-DECISION-013**, and relationships in the history's declared local event order against committed Decisions and earlier lifecycle events. Decision withdrawal targets and Decision supersession targets/successors MUST resolve uniquely within that scope; supersession target and successor MUST be distinct. A withdrawal or Decision supersession target MUST NOT already be withdrawn or superseded. Requirement supersession target and successor references MUST remain in that same context and exact subject, their Requirement identifiers MUST be distinct, and a Requirement MUST NOT be superseded twice. Invalid evidence MUST use `FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_DECISION` without changing either history. Requirement references MUST remain opaque; this rule MUST NOT require an absent Requirement registry or infer event order from timestamps.
APPROVAL-VALIDITY-014.title: APPROVAL-VALIDITY-014

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-015.statement: Before successfully recording a Decision, an implementation MUST validate retained lifecycle relationships against the complete proposed resulting Decision history under APPROVAL-VALIDITY-014. The candidate MUST match its supplied Requirement exactly under **APPROVAL-DECISION-013**, while retained Decisions for other Requirements MAY remain only when they share that Requirement's context and exact subject. The new Decision MUST NOT duplicate a Decision identity anywhere in that context, make a retained withdrawal target or Decision supersession target or successor ambiguous, or otherwise invalidate a required historical relationship. Such a record request MUST fail with `FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_DECISION` and MUST preserve both input histories without exposing a partial append. Equal Decision reference tuples alone MUST NOT be rejected by this rule when they invalidate no retained relationship.
APPROVAL-VALIDITY-015.title: APPROVAL-VALIDITY-015

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-016.statement: A concrete Decision or Decision-history input MUST NOT accept a caller-supplied `effective` member as current-effectiveness evidence. Current effectiveness MUST be derived under APPROVAL-VALIDITY-001 from the governing Decision, lifecycle, fact or revision, eligibility, expiration, and explicit-context evidence. Any supplied `effective` member at a concrete boundary, including Boolean `true` or `false`, MUST use `FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_DECISION` and MUST leave committed Decision and lifecycle history unchanged. This prohibition does not apply to Approval Composition's separately documented lightweight current-effectiveness observation fixture.
APPROVAL-VALIDITY-016.title: APPROVAL-VALIDITY-016

APPROVAL-VALIDITY-017.statement: In the stronger bounded lifecycle contract, a Decision withdrawal or supersession reference MUST identify a committed Decision by a `decisionRef` containing its nonempty `contextId` and `decisionId`; Decision supersession MUST separately identify the successor by `successorDecisionRef`. Decision references MUST use the one history context and resolve exactly once within it. When a withdrawal boundary supplies the affected Requirement, that Requirement MUST match the target Decision's scoped Requirement association exactly. Requirement supersession MUST use scoped `requirementRef` and `successorRequirementRef` values with the same history context and exact subject, distinct nonempty Requirement identities, and no inference from a registry. Decision-supersession target and successor MAY identify different Requirements within that scope; no approval transfers between them. A missing, malformed, foreign-context, foreign-subject, unresolved, duplicate-identity, already withdrawn, or already superseded reference MUST use `FINKORE_APPROVAL_INVALID_DECISION` and preserve both histories. Lifecycle identity MUST NOT fall back to facts, bare Requirement identifiers, Actor/timestamp tuples, timestamp order, or first-match selection.
APPROVAL-VALIDITY-017.title: APPROVAL-VALIDITY-017

AUDIT-REDACTION-008.statement: A redaction policy identifier is optional. In the bounded policy representation, `policy.id` MAY be omitted; when supplied, it MUST be a nonempty string. Supplied null, empty strings and non-string values MUST be rejected with `FINKORE_AUDIT_REDACTION_INVALID` during policy validation, before candidate evidence validation. An omitted identifier MUST NOT prevent otherwise valid redaction. An identifier MUST NOT substitute for required authority or protected targets, change which content is redacted, or authorize changes to committed history. Rejection MUST leave logical history unchanged under **AUDIT-ERROR-001**.
AUDIT-REDACTION-008.title: AUDIT-REDACTION-008

AUDIT-REDACTION-009.statement: A bounded redaction request MUST supply a top-level, nonempty string `sourceEventId` that selects exactly one already committed Audit Event in the supplied logical history. Every protected target declared by the policy MUST resolve within that selected Event. An omitted, null, empty, non-string, unknown, or ambiguous `sourceEventId`, or a protected target absent from the selected Event, MUST fail with `FINKORE_AUDIT_REDACTION_INVALID`. The request MUST NOT select, combine, or redact content from another Event, and failure MUST leave the complete logical history unchanged.
AUDIT-REDACTION-009.title: AUDIT-REDACTION-009

AUDIT-REDACTION-010.statement: The candidate redaction evidence Event MUST contain an object-valued `metadata.redactionEvidence` with the selected `sourceEventId`, the policy `authority`, and the exact ordered `protectedTargets` supplied by the policy. It MUST also contain `policyId` exactly when the policy supplies `id`, with the same value. The candidate Event's Entity reference MUST match the selected source Event's Entity reference, and the evidence MUST NOT contain a protected source value. Missing, malformed, partial, additional, or mismatched linkage MUST fail with `FINKORE_AUDIT_REDACTION_INVALID` after intrinsic candidate Event validation. Existing invalid-Event, invalid-Actor, duplicate-event, and Audit Relationship failures retain their existing portable codes and precedence. Rejection MUST leave logical history unchanged.

AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-003.statement: The permitted Audit Relationship types are exactly `CORRECTS`, `REVERSES`, `VOIDS`, and `SUPERSEDES`. An implementation MUST NOT silently accept, normalize, or reinterpret another relationship type as one of these values.

AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-004.statement: A source Audit Event MUST NOT target itself through an Audit Relationship.

AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-005.statement: A committed logical Audit history MUST NOT contain two Audit Relationships with the same relationship identity.

AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-006.statement: Appending an Audit Event with an Audit Relationship whose target Audit Event is not already committed in the supplied logical history MUST fail with `FINKORE_AUDIT_INVALID_EVENT` and MUST NOT commit the source event.

AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-009.statement: Audit Relationships MUST be preserved as committed event content by later appends; later events MUST NOT rewrite, reorder, remove, or reinterpret committed relationships.

AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-010.statement: A redacted Audit Event representation MUST preserve Audit Relationship identity, type, target event identity, and target Entity reference unless a future redaction rule explicitly defines a safe relationship redaction mechanism.

AUDIT-RELATIONSHIP-013.statement: An invalid, missing, malformed, unsupported, duplicate, unknown-target, self-targeting, or target-Entity-mismatched Audit Relationship MUST fail with `FINKORE_AUDIT_INVALID_EVENT` unless the primary failure is an existing append-only, duplicate-event, redaction, or actor failure.

CORE-001.1.statement: A monetary value SHALL contain an exact base-10 amount and a currency. An amount SHALL NOT be interpreted as monetary value without its currency.
CORE-001.1.title: Amount and currency are inseparable

CORE-001.2.statement: Where a monetary calculation has an exactly representable result, it SHALL preserve that result. Precision reduction SHALL use a declared rounding rule and SHALL NOT select a rounding method or target scale implicitly.
CORE-001.2.title: Exact calculation and explicit rounding

CORE-001.3.statement: Monetary amounts SHALL be added, subtracted, ordered, or treated as numerically equal only when their currencies are compatible. Conversion SHALL be explicit; incompatibility SHALL NOT be silently resolved.
CORE-001.3.title: Incompatible currencies are not combined or compared

CORE-001.4.statement: An allocation SHALL preserve the source currency and return results whose exact sum equals the source amount. It SHALL NOT drop, duplicate, create, or destroy allocation units.
CORE-001.4.title: Allocation conserves the source value

CORE-002.1.statement: Where a financial subject has a lifecycle, it SHALL have one declared current state. Its state SHALL change only through a declared transition from that state after all applicable conditions have passed.
CORE-002.1.title: Lifecycle changes require a declared valid transition

CORE-002.2.statement: A proposed financial change SHALL be evaluated against the complete proposed result and declared relevant facts before it becomes observable. Validation or transition-condition evaluation SHALL NOT itself alter domain data.
CORE-002.2.title: Validation is complete, fact-based, and non-mutating

CORE-002.3.statement: A rejected financial action SHALL leave relevant observable financial state, financial data, and committed history unchanged, unless a governing rule expressly defines another failure effect.
CORE-002.3.title: Rejected actions have no partial financial effect

CORE-002.4.statement: For a subject with state-dependent mutability, the governing domain SHALL declare which fields may change in each state. A change targeting an immutable field SHALL be rejected.
CORE-002.4.title: Mutability is declared by state and field

CORE-003.1.statement: A committed financial event SHALL preserve a stable event identity, declared event type, affected financial subject, and unambiguous occurrence time. It SHALL identify the responsible actor when known.
CORE-003.1.title: A committed event preserves essential evidence

CORE-003.2.statement: A committed financial-history event and an explicitly recorded ordering relationship SHALL NOT be replaced, modified, removed, or silently reordered.
CORE-003.2.title: Committed history is not destructively rewritten

CORE-003.3.statement: A correction, reversal, void, or supersession SHALL preserve a verifiable relationship to the affected original subject or event. It SHALL NOT erase or rewrite original financial facts or history, and these concepts SHALL NOT be silently treated as interchangeable.
CORE-003.3.title: Corrections and related evolution preserve original facts

CORE-003.4.statement: Financial-history content MAY be redacted only under identified policy or authority. Redaction SHALL remain distinguishable from original absence and preserve the event identity, type, affected subject, occurrence time, actor attribution, and recorded relationships needed to evidence the event.
CORE-003.4.title: Redaction preserves evidence of history

CORE-004.1.statement: An approval requirement SHALL identify the subject requiring approval, eligible decision-maker or eligibility rule, and the outcome that satisfies or rejects it. Eligibility SHALL be evaluated independently from technical ability to submit a request.
CORE-004.1.title: Approval requirements state subject, eligibility, and outcome

CORE-004.2.statement: An approval condition SHALL be evaluated against identified domain facts. If a required fact is absent, the requirement SHALL fail or remain unresolved; it SHALL NOT be silently treated as not applicable.
CORE-004.2.title: Missing facts do not create an approval exemption

CORE-004.3.statement: An approval decision SHALL identify its requirement, deciding actor, outcome, time, and relevant subject facts or state. It SHALL NOT be assumed valid after relevant facts change, and a committed decision SHALL NOT be overwritten or removed from logical approval history.
CORE-004.3.title: Decisions remain tied to their facts and history

CORE-004.4.statement: An approval chain SHALL declare whether its applicable requirements are sequential or unordered. It SHALL be approved only when every applicable requirement is approved; it SHALL remain pending while an applicable requirement is pending unless an effective rejection determines the declared outcome.
CORE-004.4.title: Chain status follows declared requirements and decisions

CORE-005.1.statement: A continuing financial subject SHALL have an identifier unique within its declared scope and stable throughout its lifecycle. Distinct subjects SHALL NOT share that identifier within the same scope.
CORE-005.1.title: Continuing financial subjects retain stable identity

CORE-005.2.statement: Where the governing domain gives materially different meaning to absence, an explicit null, an unknown actor, a redacted value, a pending approval, a rejected approval, a not-applicable requirement, or zero monetary amount, those conditions SHALL remain distinguishable.
CORE-005.2.title: Materially distinct conditions remain distinguishable

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-001.statement: Recording Entity evolution MUST NOT change the stable identity of any continuing Financial Entity.

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-002.statement: When a composing domain uses Entity Revisions, each Revision identity MUST identify a particular declared Entity observation or version, MUST be stable within its revision scope, and MUST remain distinct from stable Entity identity.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-002.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-002

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-003.statement: When a composing domain uses Evolution Relations, each relation identity MUST identify the relationship itself, MUST be stable within its relation scope, and MUST NOT be treated as the identity of the source or related Entity.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-003.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-003

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-004.statement: Correction, Reversal, Void, and Supersession MUST be treated as distinct evolution concepts; an implementation MUST NOT silently treat one successful or failed evolution kind as another.

coverage.scope_note: Absence of unstandardized Replacement/Amendment operations is enforced by API and registry review.

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-005.statement: Replacement and Amendment MUST NOT be treated as portable Core 2.0 evolution operations unless a composing specification explicitly defines their meaning and maps them to one or more portable evolution concepts.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-005.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-005

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-006.statement: Workflow State names, terminal-state status, or display labels such as final, approved, posted, void, reversed, corrected, or superseded MUST NOT by themselves establish evolution eligibility or financial finality. Eligibility and consequences MUST be declared by the composing domain or lifecycle policy.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-006.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-006

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-007.statement: An evolution request MUST identify one source Financial Entity, exactly one supported evolution kind, and every related Entity, Revision, or Evolution Relation required by that kind.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-007.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-007

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-008.statement: A Correction MUST preserve the source Entity's stable identity and original financial facts while producing or identifying a corrected related Entity or Revision carrying the corrected financial facts.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-008.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-008

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-009.statement: A Correction MUST NOT mutate source financial facts in place when the composing domain or lifecycle policy declares those facts no longer directly mutable.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-009.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-009

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-010.statement: A Correction request MUST be rejected when the source Entity is not eligible for correction under the composing domain or lifecycle policy.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-010.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-010

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-011.statement: A Reversal MUST preserve the source Entity's stable identity and original financial facts while producing or identifying a reversing related Entity or Revision whose cancelling or opposite effect is defined by the composing domain.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-011.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-011

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-012.statement: A Reversal MUST NOT erase, overwrite, or negate source financial facts in place.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-012.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-012

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-013.statement: When a Correction or Reversal creates or references a related Financial Entity, that related Entity MUST have a stable identity supplied or preserved according to the Entity identity requirements; the implementation MUST NOT infer that identity from mutable source facts.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-013.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-013

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-014.statement: A Correction or Reversal request that would duplicate an existing Evolution Relation identity or violate the composing domain's declared duplicate policy MUST be rejected without creating another relation.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-014.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-014

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-015.statement: Original financial facts relevant to a corrected or reversed source Entity MUST remain observable after the successful Correction or Reversal.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-015.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-015

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-016.statement: A Void MUST represent source nullification without deleting the source Entity.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-016.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-016

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-017.statement: A Void MUST NOT remove source identity, source financial facts, or prior evolution and audit evidence.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-017.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-017

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-018.statement: A Void request MUST be rejected when the source Entity is not eligible to be voided under the composing domain or lifecycle policy.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-018.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-018

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-019.statement: A Supersession MUST relate a predecessor Entity or Revision to a successor Entity or Revision without changing either stable Entity identity.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-019.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-019

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-020.statement: Within the composing domain's declared supersession scope, a successfully superseded predecessor MUST NOT be represented as the current Entity or Revision after supersession succeeds.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-020.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-020

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-021.statement: A Supersession MUST preserve predecessor financial facts and history; it MUST NOT rewrite the predecessor to match the successor.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-021.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-021

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-022.statement: A successful evolution operation MUST leave an observable evolution history or relationship observation that identifies the evolution kind, source Entity identity, related Entity or Revision identity when applicable, and Evolution Relation identity when supplied.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-022.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-022

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-023.statement: A rejected evolution request MUST leave source Entity identity, related Entity identity, current lifecycle State, data, Revision identity or currentness, and existing Evolution Relations unchanged.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-023.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-023

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-034.statement: When validating required evolution Audit evidence, an implementation MUST apply Audit validation in the order defined by `AUDIT-ERROR-004` before selecting an evolution-correspondence error. If Audit validation succeeds but required evolution correspondence fails, the request MUST fail with `FINKORE_ENTITY_INVALID_MUTATION`. Either failure MUST NOT produce a partial evolution or Audit result.

ENTITY-EVOLUTION-035.statement: An implementation MUST reject an evolution request whose supplied or resulting evolution history contains unresolved contradictory currentness observations as defined in the Portable Model with `FINKORE_ENTITY_INVALID_MUTATION`, without selecting an arbitrary winner or changing any supplied Entity, Revision, currentness, evolution-history, or Audit-history observation. It MUST validate supplied-history consistency independently of whether an expected-currentness precondition is supplied and before comparing that expectation with observed currentness. It MUST NOT reject a consistent history solely because declared evolution effects change currentness between historical steps.
ENTITY-EVOLUTION-035.title: ENTITY-EVOLUTION-035

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-001.statement: A Financial Entity MUST declare or reference a [Workflow](../workflow/README.md).
ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-001.title: ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-001

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-002.title: ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-002

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-004.statement: Audit requirements for lifecycle Transitions MUST be declared as specified by [Financial Entities](README.md).
ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-004.title: ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-004

coverage.scope_note: State consequences are defined by concrete composing domains, not generic Entity Core.

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-005.statement: A composing domain MUST define the domain consequences of each state.

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-006.statement: A Financial Entity MUST have exactly one current lifecycle State.
ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-006.title: ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-006

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-007.statement: In the bounded Entity representation, an existing observation's missing, null, empty, or non-string current State MUST use `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_INSTANCE`. A nonempty string identifying an undeclared State MUST use `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_STATE`. Consuming Entity operations MUST preserve Workflow validation priority under **WORKFLOW-ERROR-007**, including definition validation before instance validation, and MUST preserve existing observations on failure.
ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-007.title: ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-007

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-008.statement: When a bounded Entity Transition Request supplies object-valued guard facts, the Entity transition MUST pass that exact value to the referenced Workflow Transition Guard evaluation. Omission MUST represent no supplied facts. The operation MUST NOT derive guard facts implicitly from Entity data, Approval history, authorization services, wall-clock state, or other ambient state. Supplied facts MUST NOT create a Guard where the referenced Workflow declares none, and failed guard evaluation MUST preserve the complete Entity and supplied facts.
ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-008.title: ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-008

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-009.statement: In Core 2.0, a supplied Entity Transition `facts` value MUST be an object. A supplied null, array, string, number, or Boolean MUST fail with `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_CONTEXT` according to **WORKFLOW-ERROR-008**. Omission continues to mean that no facts were supplied. The error and preservation semantics are part of the Core 2.0 contract for the existing canonical `finkore.entity.transition` operation; no alias or replacement operation is introduced.
ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-009.title: ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-009

MONEY-ALLOCATION-001.statement: An allocation request MUST provide a valid source Money value, exactly one supported allocation method, and an explicit target scale. Required allocation request members MUST NOT be omitted or null.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-001.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-001

MONEY-ALLOCATION-002.statement: The target scale MUST be a non-negative integer and MUST NOT be inferred from currency metadata, locale, source amount scale, or implementation defaults.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-002.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-002

MONEY-ALLOCATION-003.statement: Equal-part allocation MUST declare a positive integer part count and MUST return exactly that many Money values in declared order.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-003.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-003

MONEY-ALLOCATION-004.statement: Ratio allocation MUST declare a non-empty ordered list of positive integer ratios and MUST return exactly one Money value for each ratio in declared order.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-004.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-004

MONEY-ALLOCATION-005.statement: Zero and negative source Money amounts MUST be valid allocation sources and MUST follow ordinary signed numeric semantics.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-005.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-005

MONEY-ALLOCATION-006.statement: Before distributing units, the source amount MUST be exactly representable as an integer number of allocation units at the target scale; otherwise allocation MUST fail with `FINKORE_MONEY_ROUNDING_REQUIRED` and MUST NOT round the source total.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-006.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-006

MONEY-ALLOCATION-007.statement: Every allocated Money value MUST preserve the source Money currency.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-007.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-007

MONEY-ALLOCATION-008.statement: The exact numeric sum of all allocated Money values MUST equal the exact source Money amount; allocation MUST NOT drop, duplicate, create, or destroy allocation units.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-008.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-008

MONEY-ALLOCATION-009.statement: Allocation MUST distribute the absolute number of source allocation units across declared weights using exact integer arithmetic. Equal-part allocation uses weight `1` for each part; ratio allocation uses each declared positive integer ratio as its weight. Each base allocation is the floor of `absolute source units * position weight / total weight`, and the distributable remainder is the absolute source unit count minus the sum of those base allocations.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-009.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-009

MONEY-ALLOCATION-010.statement: When the absolute unit count is not evenly divisible by the total declared weight, remainder allocation units MUST be assigned one unit at a time to the earliest declared result positions until no remainder remains.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-010.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-010

MONEY-ALLOCATION-011.statement: For a negative source amount, remainder assignment MUST use the same declared order and increase the magnitude of the affected negative allocated results.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-011.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-011

MONEY-ALLOCATION-012.statement: Allocation MUST be deterministic for the same source Money, allocation method, declared order, and target scale.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-012.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-012

MONEY-ALLOCATION-013.statement: Allocation MUST NOT alter the observable value of the source Money operand, whether allocation succeeds or fails.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-013.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-013

MONEY-ALLOCATION-014.statement: Every allocation target scale, equal-part count, and ratio MUST be a finite JSON number whose mathematical value is an integer. A target scale MUST be from `0` through `50` inclusive, an equal-part count MUST be from `1` through `100` inclusive, and each ratio MUST be from `1` through `9007199254740991` inclusive. JSON strings, booleans, nulls, non-integer numbers, non-finite implementation values, and integers outside the applicable range MUST be rejected with `FINKORE_MONEY_INVALID_ALLOCATION`.
MONEY-ALLOCATION-014.title: MONEY-ALLOCATION-014

Unsupported or mutable numeric objects, including unsupported subclasses of supported numeric classes, MUST fail definition construction/import with `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_DEFINITION` before they can alter retained semantics. Supported exact numeric values MUST be preserved without conversion through binary floating point or arbitrary numeric string coercion. Failure MUST leave existing instances and their bindings unchanged, and MUST follow WORKFLOW-ERROR-007's definition-first priority.
WORKFLOW-GUARD-007.title: WORKFLOW-GUARD-007

WORKFLOW-IMPORT-001.statement: Workflow Import MUST use the caller-supplied Imported Current State. It MUST NOT infer the current State from the definition's initial State, declaration order, terminal States, transition history, or implementation defaults.
WORKFLOW-IMPORT-001.title: WORKFLOW-IMPORT-001

WORKFLOW-IMPORT-002.statement: Workflow Import MUST validate that the Imported Current State is declared by the supplied Workflow definition or by the supplied Workflow Definition Version for a versioned instance.
WORKFLOW-IMPORT-002.title: WORKFLOW-IMPORT-002

WORKFLOW-IMPORT-003.statement: Workflow Import of a versioned instance MUST include exactly one Bound Workflow Definition Version and MUST validate that it exactly matches the supplied Workflow Definition Identity and Workflow Definition Version Identity.
WORKFLOW-IMPORT-003.title: WORKFLOW-IMPORT-003

WORKFLOW-IMPORT-004.statement: Workflow Import MUST preserve the supplied Bound Workflow Definition Version and any supplied Imported Workflow Instance Revision as opaque values. It MUST NOT normalize, generate, derive, increment, or reinterpret either value from storage counters, Entity Revision, timestamps, transition counts, or current State.
WORKFLOW-IMPORT-004.title: WORKFLOW-IMPORT-004

WORKFLOW-IMPORT-005.statement: A successful Workflow Import MUST return an observation with the supplied current State, Bound Workflow Definition Version when versioned, and Imported Workflow Instance Revision when supplied. It MUST NOT perform a Transition Request, evaluate Transition Guards, create Audit evidence, or claim that a State change occurred.
WORKFLOW-IMPORT-005.title: WORKFLOW-IMPORT-005

WORKFLOW-IMPORT-006.statement: A failed Workflow Import MUST NOT return a partially imported instance and MUST NOT change any existing Workflow instance observation.
WORKFLOW-IMPORT-006.title: WORKFLOW-IMPORT-006

WORKFLOW-STATES-001.statement: Each state MUST have an identifier unique within its workflow definition.
WORKFLOW-STATES-001.title: WORKFLOW-STATES-001

WORKFLOW-STATES-002.statement: A Workflow definition MUST declare exactly one initial State.
WORKFLOW-STATES-002.title: WORKFLOW-STATES-002

WORKFLOW-STATES-003.statement: A newly created Workflow instance MUST begin in the declared initial State. Importing an instance with existing history is a separate operation whose resulting State MUST be defined by the composing specification.
WORKFLOW-STATES-003.title: WORKFLOW-STATES-003

WORKFLOW-STATES-004.statement: The current state MUST be one of the declared states.
WORKFLOW-STATES-004.title: WORKFLOW-STATES-004

WORKFLOW-STATES-005.statement: State identifiers MUST be treated as domain names, not presentation labels.
WORKFLOW-STATES-005.title: WORKFLOW-STATES-005

WORKFLOW-STATES-008.statement: The bounded portable Workflow definition MUST explicitly supply its terminal-State and Transition collections, including when either collection is empty. Omission, null, or a non-array collection MUST use `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_DEFINITION`. Native convenience constructors MAY supply documented empty defaults, but portable parsing MUST preserve the distinction between omission and an explicit empty collection.
WORKFLOW-STATES-008.title: WORKFLOW-STATES-008

WORKFLOW-STATES-009.statement: Every portable Workflow State identifier MUST be a nonempty string, including identifiers in the declared State collection, initial and terminal State declarations, Transition endpoints, a Workflow instance's current State, a requested target State, and an expected-current-State precondition. An empty identifier in a definition MUST use `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_DEFINITION`; an empty current State in an instance MUST use `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_INSTANCE`; and an empty requested target or expected-current-State precondition MUST use `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_STATE`. Existing error priority and failure non-mutation requirements continue to apply. Nonempty State identifiers remain opaque and case-sensitive.
WORKFLOW-STATES-009.title: WORKFLOW-STATES-009

WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-001.statement: A Workflow definition MUST explicitly identify each terminal State.
WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-001.title: WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-001

WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-002.statement: A terminal State MUST NOT have an outgoing Transition in that Workflow definition.

WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-003.statement: A Transition Request from a terminal State MUST fail with `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_TERMINAL_STATE`.

WORKFLOW-TERMINAL-004.statement: Terminal status MUST be determined from the Workflow definition, not inferred from naming.

WORKFLOW-TRANSITION-001.statement: A Transition MUST identify one declared Source State and one declared Target State.

WORKFLOW-TRANSITION-002.statement: A Transition is directed; declaring one direction MUST NOT declare or permit its reverse.

WORKFLOW-TRANSITION-003.statement: A Transition Request MUST match a Transition whose Source State is the instance's current State.

WORKFLOW-VERSION-001.statement: A versioned Workflow Definition MUST declare exactly one Workflow Definition Identity and exactly one Workflow Definition Version Identity.

WORKFLOW-VERSION-002.statement: Workflow Definition Identity and Workflow Definition Version Identity values MUST be stable opaque identifiers supplied by the caller or composing domain. A FinKore implementation MUST NOT derive their meaning from database counters, timestamps, storage row identifiers, state names, transition lists, deployment artifact names, Entity identity, or Entity Revision.

coverage.scope_note: An isolated JSON request cannot prove identity non-reuse across publications or retained caller aliases. Consumers must verify retained ownership with native tests. Cross-publication identity reuse still requires a consumer registry or history.

WORKFLOW-VERSION-003.statement: Within one Workflow Definition Identity, a Workflow Definition Version Identity MUST identify exactly one immutable declared definition version. The same version identity MUST NOT be reused for different declared state, transition, guard, or terminal-state semantics.
WORKFLOW-VERSION-003.title: WORKFLOW-VERSION-003

WORKFLOW-VERSION-004.statement: Workflow Definition Version Identity MUST remain distinct from Entity Revision, Entity identity, database row version, optimistic-lock token, storage counter, and storage timestamp unless a composing specification explicitly defines one value as immutably carrying both meanings.

WORKFLOW-VERSION-007.statement: A versioned Workflow instance MUST record exactly one Bound Workflow Definition Version when the instance is created, imported, or otherwise observed as an existing instance.
WORKFLOW-VERSION-007.title: WORKFLOW-VERSION-007

WORKFLOW-VERSION-008.statement: A Workflow instance's Bound Workflow Definition Version MUST be immutable for that instance's lifecycle unless a future FinKore migration operation explicitly changes it. A Transition Request MUST NOT change the binding.
WORKFLOW-VERSION-008.title: WORKFLOW-VERSION-008

WORKFLOW-VERSION-009.statement: Transition validation for a versioned Workflow instance MUST use the states, transitions, guards, and terminal-state declarations of the instance's Bound Workflow Definition Version, not a newer or different version under the same Workflow Definition Identity.
WORKFLOW-VERSION-009.title: WORKFLOW-VERSION-009

WORKFLOW-VERSION-010.statement: If a versioned Workflow operation is supplied a Workflow Definition whose identity or version identity does not exactly match the instance's Bound Workflow Definition Version, the operation MUST fail with `FINKORE_WORKFLOW_VERSION_MISMATCH` and MUST leave the current State and binding unchanged.
WORKFLOW-VERSION-010.title: WORKFLOW-VERSION-010

WORKFLOW-VERSION-011.statement: An instance bound to an older Workflow Definition Version MUST remain governed by that older version while its current State belongs to that bound version, even when a newer version changes state declarations, transition declarations, guard declarations, or terminal-state declarations.
